THEOREM A. For a<b with {a,b} subset M and M' = M\{a,b}: Atilde_{M,I} = rho * Atilde_{M',I} mod (w_a w_b - 1) for EVERY I, with rho = (1-q)^2/((1-q w_a^2)(1-q w_a^{-2})) independent of M, of I, of the branch index K, and of N. Proof: in Motegi's branching formula the label I occurs only inside Phi_{K,I} = W_{N,r}(w_K|w|I)/prod(1-q w_k^{-1} w_k') * prod(1-w_k^{-1} w_k'^{-1}), which depends on (K,I) alone; the remaining factors Psi depend on (K,L,M^c) alone. Terms with K meeting {a,b} vanish on H by long-root-order-lemma, so the surviving index set is exactly that of M'. On H, w_b = w_a^{-1}, and EVERY factor with ONE leg in {a,b} is accompanied by its own image under w_a <-> w_b, so four ratios collapse to 1: the K-dependence (h(k) = 1), the L-dependence (Pi_4 against Pi_5), the M^c-dependence (Pi_5 against Pi_1), and (1-q w_a^{-1} w_b^{-1}) = (1-q) = (1-q w_a w_b). What survives is the one factor with BOTH legs in {a,b}, against the leading (1-q)^{|L|}. Verified independently on the brute-force S_n engine (which never uses the branching formula): 48/48 at N=3 type C over a 12-item non-degenerate domain (the type B arm formerly cited here, 48/48, is RETRACTED 2026-10-17: it normalised WB by E^C -- see typeB-multiplier-corrected. The TYPE C claim is unaffected); plant rho -> rho(1+q) fails 12/12 and plant rho -> 1 (the untwisted/collision reading) fails 12/12, on exactly that domain and nowhere else. SO: a long-root divisor IS a collapse, twisted by a scalar. Q488's 'the long-root divisors are not collision divisors ... this is the whole asymmetry' has the right conclusion and an incomplete reason -- the specialisation POINTS do not collide, but the ROWS do, projectively. | AMENDED 2026-10-17: the sentence 'the same statement and the same rho hold in type B' is withdrawn. The STATEMENT holds in type B; the MULTIPLIER does not. rho is type-dependent: rho^X = (1-q)^2/((1-q w_a^h)(1-q w_b^h)) with h = 2 (type C, long root 2t_c) and h = 1 (type B, short root t_c). children.statement: THEOREM. The '<=' half of exact-pole-divisor, previously only conjectured. Say kappa BRACKETS (a,b) if {a,b} subset kappa and kappa\{a,b} >= lambda and >= mu. If NO kappa with nu >= kappa >= lambda, kappa >= mu brackets (a,b), then ord_{H_ab} c^nu >= 0. Proof by induction along a linear extension. The hypothesis is inherited downward by transitivity of Motegi's order. If {a,b} not subset nu then ord_H Atilde_{nu,nu} = 0 and every term of the recursion is regular. If {a,b} subset nu, the hypothesis at kappa = nu gives nu' = nu\{a,b} not>= lambda (wlog), so long-root-order-lemma makes ord_H Atilde_{nu,lambda} >= 1; and for every contributing kappa we have kappa >= lambda, so nu' >= kappa would give nu' >= lambda by TRANSITIVITY -- contradiction -- hence nu' not>= kappa and ord_H Atilde_{nu,kappa} >= 1 as well. Both terms beat ord_H Atilde_{nu,nu} = 1. This strictly generalises laurent-criterion-if-direction, which is the case where jump-equals-pair-deletion makes the hypothesis hold for every pair at once; the point of the generalisation is that it is available DIVISOR BY DIVISOR, which is what the minimality argument of created-pole-residue consumes.

(1) I intended to read the bidegree off Motegi's symmetrisation formula, where each w_k occurs only in linear factors, one per POSITION j, and sigma does not move positions -- so every sigma-term has the same bidegree (n - [a in I], n - [b in I]). A corner argument must be applied to Atilde divided by its manifestly H-nonvanishing factors, and I have no clean description of those in the unequal-cardinality case.
